business_model.basis: stated directly in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business) and P3 (10-K MD&A Company Overview)
business_model.claim: Pagaya is an AI-powered lending technology company that connects financial institutions (Partners) with institutional investors, processing loan applications across personal loans, auto loans, point-of-sale, and single-family rental asset classes.
quotes: We have built and continue to enhance a network connecting financial institutions and their customers with investors, which is designed to facilitate greater access to financial products and services for consumers. Our business began in personal loans and has expanded to auto loans, point-of-sale and single-family rental ("SFR").

We are a product-focused technology company that deploys sophisticated data science and proprietary, AI-powered technology to enable better outcomes for financial institutions, their existing and potential customers, and institutional or sophisticated investors.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P3 and P4
business_model.claim: Pagaya's revenue is derived from four streams: network AI fees (AI integration fees and capital markets execution fees), contract fees (management, performance, and administration fees), interest income from risk retention holdings and cash balances, and investment income from ownership interests in Financing Vehicles.
quotes: We generate revenue from network AI fees, contract fees, interest income and investment income. Revenue from fees is comprised of network AI fees and contract fees. Network AI fees can be further broken down into two fee streams, including AI integration fees and capital markets execution fees.

We also earn interest income from our investments in loans and securities, including risk retention holdings and additional investments we may make in our sponsored asset backed securitizations, and from our corporate cash balances. We earn investment income associated with our ownership interests in certain investment fund where Pagaya is the Registered Investment Advisor ("RIA") and other proprietary investments.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P3, P4, and F2
business_model.claim: Production Costs are the dominant cost line and are highly correlated to Network Volume, as they compensate Partners for acquiring and originating assets transferred into Financing Vehicles.
quotes: We incur costs when Network Volume is acquired by the Financing Vehicles. These costs, which we refer to as ''Production Costs,'' compensate our Partners for acquiring and originating assets. Accordingly, the amount and growth of our Production Costs are highly correlated to Network Volume.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P8 (Q3 2026 earnings release) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: FRLPC (Fee Revenue Less Production Costs) is the key non-GAAP operating metric Pagaya uses to assess its core profitability, and it contracted to 4.1% of Network Volume in Q3 2026, down 91 basis points year-over-year due to higher benchmark rates.
quotes: Revenue from fees less production costs ("FRLPC") of $146 million in 3Q'26, increased 5% year-over- year. FRLPC as a % of network volume ("FRLPC %") contracted by 91 basis points year-over-year to 4.1%, driven by the short-term impact of higher benchmark rates.
An important operating metric to evaluate the success of our economic model, therefore, is FRLPC, or Fee Revenue Less Production Costs.
